purpose: evidence that the download and extraction stages resume correctly after a hard kill, that completeness is decided by content rather than by file existence, and that the resource watchdog stops cleanly

fixture.note: the extraction tests run against a synthetic MISATO-shaped HDF5 so that a kill test could be done before the 124 GiB archive finished downloading; it uses real MISATO system ids and the same dataset names, shapes and dtypes (trajectory_coordinates (100,N,3) float32, atoms_number, molecules_begin_atom_index)

tests.target: Zenodo record 7711953 file QM.hdf5 (343,064,967 bytes) -- a real file from the same record, small enough to finish
tests.procedure: downloader launched with 16 MiB chunks and 4 workers, SIGKILL after 12 s, then restarted with identical arguments

state_at_kill.done_flags: [T,T,F,T,F,...]  (chunks 2 and 4 were in flight and correctly NOT claimed)
state_at_kill.sparse_file_real_bytes: 61 MB of a 328 MB apparent size

tests.on_restart: reported '3/21 chunks already done (0.05 GiB); 0.27 GiB remaining' and fetched only the remainder
tests.result: md5 9bc...n/a -> computed 1199f0af1eac684da3a6c2ddd0f321df == publisher md5; independent `md5sum -c` returned OK

tests.procedure: extraction of 80 systems (76 after leakage exclusions) launched with 3 workers under setsid, SIGKILL of the process group after 4 s, then restarted
tests.on_restart: reported '13 already complete {written (sha256 verified): 13}, 63 pending' and extracted exactly the 63

tests.procedure: the killed-then-resumed store was compared array by array against a separate single-pass extraction of the same 80 systems with 6 workers

tests.rationale: scripts/run_manifest_md.py decides completeness by 'output exists and is non-empty', which is exactly what a killed run leaves behind; it was shown to accept truncated 60 ps runs as complete 1 ns runs
tests.procedure: a finished 5WIJ.npz was truncated from 1,763,975 to 1,058,385 bytes (still non-empty) and the extractor re-run
tests.result: detected as incomplete (recorded size mismatch, with sha256 as the second check) and re-extracted back to 1,763,975 bytes; the other 15 systems were left alone

tests.procedure: the same --config-name re-run with --frames 50 instead of 100
tests.result: config hash changed c8ef5924f40fb8d0 -> bea626a4b74cd301 and all 76 systems became pending, so a settings change can never silently mix outputs

tests.procedure: extraction run with an impossible --min-available-gib 2000 and --watchdog-grace-seconds 5/8
tests.result: WATCHDOG PAUSE fired immediately ('system MemAvailable 989.0 GiB < floor 2000.0 GiB'), WATCHDOG STOP after the grace period, process exited 3, summary.json recorded watchdog_stop_reason, and all 9 outputs it had written verified sha256-clean with 100 frames each and zero orphan .tmp files

checks: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' in the live download process's /proc/<pid>/environ
zero nvidia file descriptors open in the download process
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps shows only two pre-existing processes, neither from this work (one owned by another user, one a pre-existing job on this account started before this session)
GPU memory unchanged from the 320/370 MiB baseline observed before any of this work started
the extractor refuses to start if torch is in sys.modules, and does not import it

caveat: the synthetic fixture's random protein cloud overlaps the ligand, so clash_warning fires on every fixture system; that is the QC detector working, not a property of real MISATO data
